title: Collections Digitization Glossary
description: Controlled glossary for the people, data, and workflows involved in digitising museum and natural-history collections.

terms.label: Accession Assessment
terms.definition: An activity with the goal of determining whether or not a specimen should be accessioned into a collection.

terms.label: Accessioning
terms.definition: The formal, documented process to legally add an object or group of objects to a museum collection. A single accession transaction occurs when one or more objects are acquired in the same manner, from one source, and at one time.
terms.source: Master Glossary for DOI Museum Property Directives

terms.label: Acquisition
terms.definition: An activity with the objective of gaining physical custody of an object for a museum collection through purchase, donation, bequest, transfer, or fieldwork. This includes the associated metadata primarily derived from primary sources.
terms.source: ISO 21246:2019(en), http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/OBI_0600008, Master Glossary for DOI Museum Property Directives
terms.scopeNote: The scope of an acquisition includes any prov:Activity that results in the possession of a specimen. In contrast, accession has a specific meaning and involves the formal transfer of ownership. Acquisition is an informal custody transfer of an object by an agent. In contrast, an accession is a formal process by which the ownership of an object is transferred to a museum

terms.label: Action
terms.definition: A semantically identifiable behavior of an entity or group of entities

terms.label: Action Specification
terms.definition: A specification composed of a sequence of instructions to achieve some objective.
terms.scopeNote: Subclass of Specification

terms.label: Activity
terms.definition: An activity is something that occurs over a period of time and acts upon or with entities; it may include consuming, processing, transforming, modifying, relocating, using, or generating entities.

terms.label: Agent
terms.definition: An agent is something that bears some form of responsibility for an activity taking place, for the existence of an entity, or for another agent's activity.
terms.scopeNote: Agents typically persons, organizations, or software that perform tasks, including making assertions, or generating information used as evidence. In the execution of such tasks, an 'agent role' is realized that inheres in the agent.

terms.label: Anthropology
terms.definition: Anthropology is the scientific study of humans, human behavior and societies in the past and present.
terms.scopeNote: Subclass of Social Sciences

terms.label: Archaeological material
terms.definition: This class represents an archaeological material, that is a part of a lot of archaeological materials.

terms.label: Archaeology
terms.definition: Archaeology, or archeology, is the study of human activity through the recovery and analysis of material culture.
terms.scopeNote: Subclass of Social Science

terms.label: Archival Resource Key
terms.definition: A resolvable URL that serves as a persistent identifier for information objects of any type Notation: ARK

terms.label: Asset
terms.definition: An asset represents the conceptual content of a resource.

terms.label: Astromaterial
terms.definition: A material entity extraterrestrial in origin or a derivative of a process involving an extraterrestrial material (impactite)

terms.label: Astromaterial Collection
terms.definition: A curated collection comprised primarily of astromaterials

terms.label: Barcode
terms.definition: Digital coding system showing an eye-visible linear array of rectangular marks of (possibly) varying width, height and vertical alignment, separated by spaces of (possibly) varying width in which the positioning and size of marks and spaces are used to code information to identify various types of material objects
terms.source: ISO 5127:2017(en) Information and documentation — Foundation and vocabulary
terms.scopeNote: Within the collections domain, the term barcode has been extended to refer to a collection-level identifier analogous to a catalog number.

terms.label: Bioinformatics Pipeline
terms.definition: A software pipeline that is composed of a wide array of software algorithms to process biological raw data.

terms.label: Biological Collection
terms.definition: A museum collection comprised predominantly of biological materials

terms.label: Biological Material
terms.definition: Material entity representative of one or more living organisms from a particular context, megascopic or microscopic
terms.source: Based on the Darwin Core term, Material Sample (http://rs.tdwg.org/dwc/terms/MaterialSample)

terms.label: Biological Object
terms.definition: Individual items (physical objects) of a material nature, which live, have lived, or are natural products of or from living organisms.
terms.source: Definition of the CIDOC Conceptual Reference Model version 7.1.3

terms.label: Biology
terms.definition: Biology is the science of life. It is concerned with the characteristics and behaviors of organisms

terms.label: Catalog Record
terms.definition: Written or electronic documentation that captures the unique identifying number assigned to a museum object or group of objects, along with a physical description, condition, provenience, and other pertinent information that facilitates physical and intellectual access.
terms.source: Master Glossary for DOI Museum Property Directives

terms.label: Collection
terms.definition: Designates an accumulated group of objects with a focal characteristic that is assembled and maintained by an agent over time.

terms.label: Collection Management
terms.definition: All practices and procedures implemented by a museum in acquiring, documenting, handling, accessing, cataloguing, storing, securing, lending, conserving and disposing of collection objects

terms.label: Collection Management System
terms.definition: An integrated software tool with a metadata structure specifically designed for capturing, curating, preserving, and accessing data associated with museum collections

terms.label: Collection Object
terms.definition: A physical or digital object that belongs to a museum collection

terms.label: Collection Workflow
terms.definition: A planned activity that defines role(s), procedures, task(s), and a specific structure in direct support of the care and digitization of museum collections
terms.scopeNote: A workflow is a type of prov:Activity that has at least two procedures as proper parts. A workflow may be seen as an abstract model of real work.

terms.label: Concept Harmonization
terms.definition: Activity leading to the establishment of a correspondence between two or more closely related or overlapping concepts having in order to eliminate or reduce minor differences between them.

terms.label: Conservator
terms.definition: Person who performs the operations necessary to maintain the integrity and value of material objects in an information and documentation organization
terms.source: ISO 5127:2017(en) Information and documentation — Foundation and vocabulary
terms.scopeNote: A collections manager is a type of conservator specifically associated with a museum collection

terms.label: Contributor
terms.definition: An entity responsible for making contributions to the resource.

terms.label: Crystallography
terms.definition: Crystallography is the scientific study of crystals.
terms.scopeNote: Subclass of Chemistry

terms.label: Cultural Heritage
terms.definition: Legacy of physical objects and intangible attributes of a group or a society that are inherited from past generations, maintained and protected in the present and preserved for future generations

terms.label: Cultural Studies
terms.definition: Cultural studies is a field of theoretically, politically, and empirically engaged cultural analysis that concentrates upon the political dynamics of contemporary culture, its historical foundations, defining traits, conflicts, and contingencies.

terms.label: Curated Holding
terms.definition: Comprises aggregations of physical objects that are curated and preserved by one or more Agents over time for a specific purpose and audience, and according to a particular collection development plan.
terms.source: Definition of the CIDOC Conceptual Reference Model version 7.1.3

terms.label: Curator
terms.definition: Person responsible for overseeing a collection with expertise in the same domain as the collection
terms.source: ISO 5127:2017(en) Information and documentation — Foundation and vocabulary

terms.label: Data Archiving
terms.definition: An activity that includes the preservation of data in a repository, archive, or a deposition database; and curation of data and metadata, database accessions, annotation, and data provenance with the goal of ensuring that data is findable and reusable.
terms.source: EDAM - Ontology of bioscientific data analysis and data management

terms.label: Data Capture
terms.definition: Deliberate action that results in the registration of a record into a record keeping system.
terms.source: ISO 18530:2021 Health informatics — Automatic identification and data capture marking and labelling — Subject of care and individual provider identification

terms.label: Data Cleaning
terms.definition: Refers to the step or series of steps for cleaning and curating data in a workflow.
terms.scopeNote: Typically these steps are undertaken by sophisticated tooling/services, or by human interactions. A Data Cleaning step preserves and enriches the content of data.

terms.label: Data Collector
terms.definition: Person/institution responsible for finding or gathering/collecting data

terms.label: Data Curation
terms.definition: A planned process in which existing data is collected, organized, and improved in preparation for subsequent use.
terms.source: Ontology for Scientific Evidence and Provenance Information

terms.label: Data Curation Workflow
terms.definition: A type of workflow that includes active steps to curate data as an aid to ongoing management of data through its lifecycle.

terms.label: Data Curator
terms.definition: Person tasked with reviewing, enhancing, cleaning, or standardizing metadata and the associated data submitted for storage, use, and maintenance within a centralized data store or repository

terms.label: Data Entry
terms.definition: The process by which original, source data is inputted by a human into a digital, structured format for later use and analysis.

terms.label: Data Governance
terms.definition: The control of data entry and maintenance to ensure the data meets defined standards, qualities, or constraints.
terms.source: EDAM - Ontology of bioscientific data analysis and data management

terms.label: Data Integration
terms.definition: Systematic combining of data from different independent and potentially heterogeneous sources, to create a more compatible, unified view of these data for research purposes
terms.source: ISO 5127:2017(en) Information and documentation — Foundation and vocabulary

terms.label: Data Lifecycle
terms.definition: Entire period of time that data exists. This life cycle describes the flow of data starting from planning, collecting, processing, analysing, preserving, sharing and finally reusing the data.

terms.label: Data Management Plan
terms.definition: Statement describing how data will be managed throughout a specified life cycle including terms regarding archiving and potential preservation of the data in a data repository. The plan is considered to be a 'living' document, i.e. one which can be updated when necessary.

terms.label: Data Manager
terms.definition: A person primarily responsible for database creation, data collection, validation, integration, coding, review, quality evaluation, and archiving, as well as for preparation of reports and data displays.

terms.label: Data Migration
terms.definition: The process of transporting data between computers, storage devices, or formats.
terms.source: Master Glossary for DOI Museum Property Directives
terms.scopeNote: Data migration is a key consideration for any system implementation, upgrade or consolidation. During data migration, software programs or scripts are used to map system data for automated migration.

terms.label: Data Mobility
terms.definition: The ability of information to be accessed and exchanged between systems

terms.label: Data Policy
terms.definition: Set of high-level principles that establish a guiding framework for data-related issues.
terms.scopeNote: A data policy may contain subsidiary sections that define approaches to strategic aspects such as data access; data protection; data management, custodianship or stewardship; data preservation; relevant legal matters; data acquisition; data ethics and other data-related issues. Distinct from a data management policy which is the subset of data policy addressing the management of a specified set of data assets.

terms.label: Data Preparation
terms.definition: Data preparation is the process of manipulating (or pre-processing) data (which may come from disparate data sources) to improve their quality or reduce bias in subsequent analysis.

terms.label: Data Product
terms.definition: A collection of one or more data items that are packaged for or by a specific application.
terms.scopeNote: A data product may have input and output ports, code and metadata

terms.label: Data Product Specification
terms.definition: Detailed description of a dataset or dataset series together with additional information that will enable it to be created, supplied to and used by another party
terms.source: ISO 19126:2021(en) Geographic information — Feature concept dictionaries and registers

terms.label: Data Profiling
terms.definition: The statistical analysis and assessment of the quality of data values within a dataset for consistency, uniqueness and logic.
terms.scopeNote: The data profiling process cannot identify inaccurate data; it can only identify business rules violations and anomalies.

terms.label: Data Provider
terms.definition: An agent or agents that produces data or reference metadata
terms.source: ISO 17369:2013(en) Statistical data and metadata exchange (SDMX)

terms.label: Data Publication Workflow
terms.definition: Activities and processes in a digital environment that lead to the publication of data, associated metadata and accompanying documentation as a web-based resource.

terms.label: Data Publishing
terms.definition: Process whereby data are subjected to an assessment process to determine whether they should be acquired by a repository; followed by a rigorous acquisition and ingest process that results in products being publicly made available and supported for the long-term by that repository.
terms.source: ISO 5127:2017(en) Information and documentation — Foundation and vocabulary

terms.label: Data Quality
terms.definition: The reliability and application efficiency of data.

terms.label: Data Steward
terms.definition: Role within an organization responsible for ensuring metadata quality, integrity, and access in a manner that is consistent with policies and practices established through data governance to ensure the data is fit for reuse.
terms.source: Adopted from ISO/TR 14872:2019 and http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/T4FS_0000178, Thomas G (2009)

terms.label: Data Transformation
terms.definition: A process whereby data is changed from one format or structure to another.

terms.label: Data Validation
terms.definition: Process used to determine if data are inaccurate, incomplete, or unreasonable.
terms.scopeNote: The process may include format checks, completeness checks, check key tests, reasonableness checks, limit checks, and checking for compliance with applicable standards, rules, and conventions.

terms.label: Dataset
terms.definition: An identifiable collection of data
terms.source: ISO 19101-1:2014(en) Geographic information — Reference model — Part 1: Fundamentals
terms.example: Data products such as images, catalogs, parameter files, calibration data, instrument characteristics, articles, and web pages

terms.label: Deaccession
terms.definition: The formal, documented process by which a museum or institution permanently removes an object from its permanent collection.
terms.source: Art Glossary: Definitions of Common Art Terms and Techniques
terms.scopeNote: An accession is guided by internal policy, professional ethics, and often oversight by governing boards or curatorial committees.

terms.label: Derivation
terms.definition: A transformation of an entity into another, an update of an entity resulting in a new one, or the construction of a new entity based on a pre-existing entity.
terms.scopeNote: For an entity to be transformed from, created from, or resulting from an update to another, there must be some underpinning activity or activities performing the necessary action(s) resulting in such a derivation.

terms.label: Determination
terms.definition: The systematic identification and classification of a collection object
terms.scopeNote: A action of making a determination is independent of the accession status of a specimen.

terms.label: Digital Collections
terms.definition: Designates an aggregation of digital objects, including digital versions of physical media, digitised resources, or born-digital items. The collection may be online presented or not.
terms.scopeNote: Disambiguates Collection terms in the LIDO ObjectType vocabulary. Here, Digital Collections are disambiguated from Physical and Online Collections

terms.label: Digital Object Identifier
terms.definition: Persistent identifiers standardized by the ISO. DOIs a re an implementation of the handle system and adhere to the URI (Universal Resource Identifier) system. Notation: DOI
terms.source: https://www.doi.org/, ISO 26324:2025 Information and documentation—Digital object identifier system

terms.label: Digitization
terms.definition: Process of converting analogue materials into digital form
terms.source: ISO 21246:2019 Information and documentation — Key indicators for museums

terms.label: Digitization Backlog
terms.definition: Accessioned collection objects for which digitization has not yet begun — meaning no specimen metadata has been captured in a collections management system or similar software.
terms.scopeNote: In the broadest sense of the term, the backlog consists of incomplete digital records, which prohibits the digitization process from advancing to the data curation and archival phase.

terms.label: Distribution
terms.definition: A specific serialized representation of a dataset.
terms.scopeNote: A dataset might be available in multiple serializations that may differ in various ways, including natural language, media-type or format, schematic organization, temporal and spatial resolution, level of detail or profiles (which might specify any or all of the above).

terms.label: Distribution Phase
terms.definition: The stage in a project when a serialized version of a mobilized dataset is made available

terms.label: Entity
terms.definition: An entity is a physical, digital, conceptual, or other kind of thing with some fixed aspects; entities may be real or imaginary.

terms.label: Environmental Science
terms.definition: Environmental science is the science of the interactions between the physical, chemical, and biological components of the environment, but with particular attention to the effects of humans on the natural environment.
terms.scopeNote: Subclass of Earth Science

terms.label: Event
terms.definition: Something that happens or occurs in time and space.
terms.source: International Council on Archives Records in Contexts Ontology (ICA RiC-O) version 1.1
terms.scopeNote: An event may be caused by nature, an agent, or a combination of nature and agent. Events have temporal and spatial boundaries. An event may actively involve some agent(s) and affect any entity. An event may be discrete, happening at a specific moment in time, or may occur over an extended period of time. Events may have events as parts, and events may precede or follow one another. Multiple agents may participate in the same event, and in different roles.

terms.label: Event Type
terms.definition: Categorization scheme for grouping events by purpose
terms.source: International Council on Archives Records in Contexts Ontology (ICA RiC-O) version 1.1
terms.scopeNote: Curation event types include creation; acquisition; transfer; arrangement; description; digitization, etc. Biographical event types include birth, marriage, death, etc.

terms.label: Extract Transform Load
terms.definition: A planned data integration process that extracts concretizations of information from a data source, prepares and transforms them, then loads the transformed concretizations into a target data store.

terms.label: FAIR Principles
terms.definition: The FAIR principles are guidelines to improve the Findability, Accessibility, Interoperability, and Reuse of digital assets. The principles emphasise machine-actionability (i.e., the capacity of computational systems to find, access, interoperate, and reuse data with none or minimal human intervention) because humans increasingly rely on computational support to deal with data as a result of the increase in volume, complexity, and creation speed of data. The principles refer to three types of entities: data (or any digital object), metadata (information about that digital object), and infrastructure.

terms.label: Feature of Interest
terms.definition: The thing being sampled or transformed in an act of sampling.

terms.label: Field
terms.definition: User-interface element in which data is entered or presented
terms.source: ISO 9241-125:2017(en) Ergonomics of human-system interaction — Part 125: Guidance on visual presentation of information

terms.label: Field Work
terms.definition: Investigation or other type of formal activity practiced by direct observation in the field as a form of primary reconnaissance
terms.source: This Document and adopted from ISO 22932-2:2020

terms.label: Format Transformation
terms.definition: A type of data transformation that preserves the content of a dataset while converting its representation format.

terms.label: Fossil
terms.definition: Any remains, trace, or imprint of a plant or animal preserved in the Earth's crust since some past geologic or prehistoric time; loosely, any evidence of past life.

terms.label: Functional Specification
terms.definition: A functional specification is a specification that describes the characteristics of an object.

terms.label: Generated
terms.definition: The completion of production of a new entity by an activity.
terms.source: W3C PROV Data Model Activity concepts
terms.scopeNote: This entity did not exist before generation and becomes available for usage after this generation. Given that a generation is the completion of production of an entity, it is instantaneous.

terms.label: Geological Collection
terms.definition: A museum collection comprised predominantly of geological materials.

terms.label: Geological Material
terms.definition: A material entity comprised of a natural amount of matter generated by some geologic process
terms.source: Adopted from GeoCore Ontology and Geosciences Ontology
terms.scopeNote: Can include minor parts that are not of geologic origin, such as organic material, and can be solid, fluid, or a mix.

terms.label: Geological Specimen
terms.definition: A collection object that is a geologic material

terms.label: Geology
terms.definition: Study of the planet earth, its composition, structure, physical and chemical processes, and history since its origin.

terms.label: Glossary
terms.definition: A collection of defined concepts within a domain

terms.label: Identifier
terms.definition: A word, number, letter, symbol, or any combination of these used to uniquely identify or reference an individual instance of an entity within a specific information domain.
terms.source: International Council on Archives Records in Contexts Ontology (ICA RiC-O) version 1.1
terms.scopeNote: Can include Global Persistent Identifiers (globally unique and persistently resolvable identifier for the entity) and/or Local Identifiers. Both the domain within which the identifier is unique, and the rules used in forming the identifier value should be provided with the identifier value.

terms.label: Identifier assignment
terms.definition: An activity that results in the allocation of an identifier that may be locally or globally unique
terms.scopeNote: Documenting the act of identifier assignment and deassignment is especially useful when objects change custody or the identification system of an organization is changed.

terms.label: Initiator
terms.definition: Something that sets into motion some course of events or causes something to happen.
terms.scopeNote: In the context of a collection workflow, an initiator starts a new procedure or branch of an existing workflow

terms.label: International Generic Sample Number
terms.definition: Globally unique, persistent and domain-agnostic identifiers for physical samples resolved through a Handle System. Mirrors the format and usage of DOIs Notation: IGSN

terms.label: Internationalized Resource Identifier
terms.definition: An internet protocol standard which builds on the Uniform Resource Identifier (URI) protocol by greatly expanding the set of permitted characters. Notation: IRI

terms.label: Iterative Workflow
terms.definition: A workflow whose steps are the repetition of the same task type.

terms.label: Kind (of)
terms.definition: A grouping of entities that share a common set of characteristics in a particular context.
terms.scopeNote: Analogous to a 'category' or classification scheme item value

terms.label: Library
terms.definition: Organization, or part of an organization, the main aim of which is to facilitate the use of such information resources, services and facilities as are required to meet the informational, research, educational, cultural or recreational needs of its users

terms.label: Life Science Identifier
terms.definition: A type of uniform resource name (URN) that conforms to the URN standards defined by the IETF. Notation: LSID

terms.label: Loan
terms.definition: The temporary transfer of custody of museum property on either a short- term (three years or less) or long-term basis.
terms.source: Master Glossary for DOI Museum Property Directives
terms.scopeNote: A loan must be for official purposes and may be incoming or outgoing. The terms of a loan are documented in a loan agreement or similar instrument.

terms.label: Local Identifier
terms.definition: Designates an assigned code that is uniquely and meaningfully defined only in the local source system or within the scope of an internal management system.
terms.scopeNote: Locally defined identifiers should not be used to establish equality between resources from separate source systems. They may be used only to compare resources coming from the same local system. They must not be considered to have meaning of their own.

terms.label: Man-made Object
terms.definition: Comprises all persistent physical objects of any size that are purposely created by human activity and have physical boundaries that separate them completely in an objective way from other objects.
terms.scopeNote: Includes all aggregates of objects made for functional purposes of whatever kind, independent of physical coherence, such as a set of chessmen.

terms.label: Material Entity
terms.definition: An entity that exists in full during the length of time of its existence, persists through this time while maintaining its identity and has no temporal parts.

terms.label: Material Sample
terms.definition: A material entity that represents an entity of interest in whole or in part dwc:MaterialSample. Top concept in material sample object type hierarchy. Represents any material sample object.

terms.label: Metadata
terms.definition: Data that defines and describes other data
terms.source: ISO/IEC 5207:2024(en) Information technology — Data usage — Terminology and use cases

terms.label: Mobilization
terms.definition: The process of preparing and transferring data from an internal resource or system to external networks for the purposes of distribution

terms.label: Module
terms.definition: A self-contained component (unit or item) that is used in combination with other components.

terms.label: Museum
terms.definition: An institution that cares for (conserves) a collection of artifacts and other objects of scientific, artistic, cultural, or historical importance.

terms.label: Museum Collection
terms.definition: An object aggregate that has as member parts a material sample that is located in a museum as a result of a process of curation.
terms.scopeNote: The class museum collection has meaning that is much broader than biological collections. It would probably be better to import this term from another, more general ontology and create a specific subclass for natural history museum collection.

terms.label: Natural Sciences
terms.definition: The natural sciences are those branches of empirical science that produce a comprehension of the natural world through the use of data collected from it by observation and measurement to construct deterministic and/or stochastic quantitative models of its phenomena.

terms.label: Online Collection
terms.definition: A virtual collection primarily designed and collocated for online presentation. The items presented in an online collection may refer to physical objects or digital resources, or both.

terms.label: Open Researcher and Contributor ID
terms.definition: A unique, persistent identifier (PID) for individuals to use as they engage in research, scholarship, and innovation activities. Notation: ORCiD

terms.label: Organization
terms.definition: An organization is a social or legal institution such as a company, society, etc.

terms.label: Paleontology
terms.definition: Study of life in past geologic time based on fossil plants and animals.

terms.label: Paleontology Collection
terms.definition: A museum collection comprised predominantly of fossils

terms.label: Parallel Workflow
terms.definition: A workflow with some tasks running concurrently.
terms.scopeNote: A workflow can be seen as a direct acyclic graph, whose nodes are tasks and edges are asymmetric causal relations. A parallel graph occurs when the topological order of such graph if not unique, meaning that there is at least one portion of the workflow in which at least two tasks are running concurrently.

terms.label: Persistent Identifier
terms.definition: A globally unique, interoperable, machine-readable and resolvable identifier that disambiguates an entity and provides long-term access to it independent of the entity's physical location or current ownership. The term denotes a general concept and is not tied to any particular standardized format (e.g., UUID).
terms.source: ISO 5127:2017(en) Information and documentation — Foundation and vocabulary

terms.label: Physical Collection
terms.definition: Designates an aggregated group of tangible objects
terms.scopeNote: Disambiguates Collection terms in the LIDO ObjectType vocabulary. Here, Physical Collections are disambiguated from Digital and Online Collections

terms.label: Physical Object
terms.definition: Items of a material nature that are units for documentation and have physical boundaries that separate them completely in an objective way from other objects.
terms.scopeNote: The decision as to what is documented as a complete item, rather than by its parts or components, may be purely administrative or may be a result of the order in which the item was acquired.
terms.example: Information about the Principal Investigator who recorded the data, and the information concerning its storage, handling, and migration.

terms.label: Data Pipeline
terms.definition: Full set of logically connected steps needed to transform input data into a result, for which one or more outputs of one data transformation step can be the input of one or more subsequent steps
terms.source: ISO/IEC 11179-34:2024(en) Information technology — Metadata registries (MDR) — Part 34: Metamodel for computable data registration

terms.label: Plan
terms.definition: An entity that represents a set of intended actions or steps executed by one or more agents to achieve some goals.

terms.label: Plan specification
terms.definition: A directive information entity with action specifications and objective specifications as parts, and that may be concretized as a realizable entity that, if realized, is realized in a process in which the bearer tries to achieve the objectives by taking the actions specified.

terms.label: Planned process
terms.definition: A process that is initiated by an agent who intends to carry out a plan to achieve an objective through one or more actions as described in a plan specification.
terms.source: Core Ontology for Biology and Biomedicine

terms.label: Preparation
terms.definition: An activity, taking place after specimen acquisition, to make a material suitable for a specific purpose such as laboratory (tissue) analysis or long-term preservation

terms.label: Preparation Object
terms.definition: The result of a process performed after specimen collection to render a material entity (collection object) suitable for a defined purpose, such as laboratory (tissue) analysis or long-term preservation.
terms.scopeNote: The term and associated definition are strictly within the scope of a museum collection and not intended for wider application.

terms.label: Preparator
terms.definition: Person carrying out the operations required for the conservation of dead animals for decoration purposes or for scientific study
terms.source: ISO 5127:2017(en) Information and documentation — Foundation and vocabulary

terms.label: Preservation
terms.definition: Act to prevent or impede biological or physical deterioration of biological material
terms.scopeNote: The term and associated definition are strictly within the scope of a biological collection and biological material.

terms.label: Primary Source
terms.definition: Materials that provide first-hand documentation or knowledge, usually of people, places, events or time periods.
terms.scopeNote: Primary sources enable the researcher to trace a research subject to its origin, potentially supporting new interpretations or revealing previously undocumented knowledge of that subject. Secondary sources build upon or extrapolate information derived from primary sources, and the distinction between the two can be quite fluid depending on one's area of study. In most contexts, however, a primary source is understood to be a point of origin, or a piece of raw data, for a research subject.

terms.label: Procedure
terms.definition: An intentional planned process performed by an agent within the context of a workflow
terms.scopeNote: An intentional process in which an agent works with some entities according to some existing formalised operative rules.

terms.label: Procedure Specification
terms.definition: A specification on the order, transitions and trigger of multiple action specifications that are part of some aggregate action specification.

terms.label: Process
terms.definition: A coordinated (parallel and/or serial) sequence of tasks that are connected in order to achieve a common goal as part of a workflow

terms.label: Process Protocol
terms.definition: A standard operating procedure (SOP) that is a collection of activities and the rules that describe when each activity is performed to achieve a specific purpose or objective(s).

terms.label: Project
terms.definition: A temporary endeavor undertaken to achieve defined objectives
terms.source: ISO 21506:2024  Project, programme and portfolio management — Vocabulary

terms.label: Project Phase
terms.definition: A collection of logically-related project activities, usually culminating in the completion of an intended goal or deliverable

terms.label: Property
terms.definition: A variable that can be considered (as an investigated property) within a processing step
terms.source: Physicalistic Interpretation of Modelling and Simulation - Interoperability Infrastructure

terms.label: Provenance
terms.definition: Information that documents the history of a described object and related described activities, and that contains information about the origin or source of the described object, any changes that can have taken place since it was originated, and who has had custody of it since it was originated
terms.source: Adopted from http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/SEPIO_0000058, Master Glossary for DOI Museum Property Directives, ISO 24480:2024(en), and http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/T4FS_0000309
terms.scopeNote: For scientific assertions/claims, this is the process history leading to the assertion being made, including the processes through which evidence is evaluated and the methods through which information used as evidence is created. The transitive nature of provenance means that the provenance history of information used as supporting data becomes provenance for an assertion that uses this information as evidence. Provenance metadata describes these processes, including accounts of who conducted them, what entities participated, and when/where they occurred.

terms.label: Provenance Statement
terms.definition: Any changes in ownership and custody of a resource since its creation that are significant for its authenticity, integrity, and interpretation.

terms.label: Quantity Kind
terms.definition: Any observable property that can be measured and quantified numerically.
terms.scopeNote: Familiar examples include physical properties such as length, mass, time, force, energy, power, electric charge, etc. Less familiar examples include currency, interest rate, price to earning ratio, and information capacity.

terms.label: Registrar
terms.definition: Person responsible for the surveilling, handling and the action(s) of physical placement of material objects in a museum
terms.source: ISO 5127:2017(en) Information and documentation — Foundation and vocabulary

terms.label: Repository
terms.definition: A Web-based resources that preserve, manage, and provide access to many types of digital materials in a variety of formats.

terms.label: Requirements
terms.definition: A proposition that states a set of conditions that have to be fulfilled to achieve some specific objective.

terms.label: Research Data Publication Workflow
terms.definition: Activities and processes in a digital environment that lead to the publication of research data, associated metadata and accompanying documentation and software code on the Web.
terms.scopeNote: In contrast to interim or final published products, workflows are the means to curate, document, and review, and thus ensure and enhance the value of the published product. Workflows can involve both humans and machines and often humans are supported by technology as they perform steps in the workflow. Similar workflows may vary in the details depending on the research discipline, data publishing product and/or the host institution of the workflow.

terms.label: Research Organization Registry Identifier
terms.definition: A ROR ID is a unique ID, expressed as a URL, that resolves to research organization's record in the ROR registry for the purposes of facilitating discovery and disambiguation.  Notation: ROR ID

terms.label: Role
terms.definition: The function of an entity or agent with respect to an activity, in the context of a usage, generation, invalidation, association, start, and end.

terms.label: Sample
terms.definition: A material entity that represents a specific known entity (feature of interest)

terms.label: Sample Collection Data Entry
terms.definition: A planned process that involves the initial entering of data about sample collection into a database.

terms.label: Semantic Interoperability
terms.definition: The capability of different information systems to communicate information consistent with the intended meaning, which encompasses the data structure elements involved, the terminology appearing as data and the associated identifiers

terms.label: Serial Workflow
terms.definition: A workflow whose tasks are carried in a sequence defined in a planned process

terms.label: Social Sciences
terms.definition: The social sciences are academic disciplines concerned with the study of the social life of human groups and individuals including anthropology, economics, geography, history, political science, psychology, social studies, and sociology.

terms.label: Source Data Verification
terms.definition: Confirming the accuracy, authenticity, and thoroughness of information by comparing it to original information and records.

terms.label: Space Science
terms.definition: Space science encompasses all of the scientific disciplines that involve space exploration and study natural phenomena and physical bodies occurring in outer space, such as space medicine and astrobiology.
terms.scopeNote: Subclass of Earth Science

terms.label: Specialized Material Entity
terms.definition: A specialized material entity is a material entity that is defined by having some quality, role or capability.

terms.label: Specification
terms.definition: A specification is a description of the essential technical attributes/requirements for an object or procedure, and may be used to determine that the object / procedure meets its requirements/attributes.

terms.label: Specimen
terms.definition: A material entity that represents a generalized population or kind of something defined within some context.
terms.scopeNote: Within the context of museum collections, specimens are collection objects commonly collected with the intent to provide information about the population or source entity it represents.

terms.label: Step
terms.definition: An atomic unit of a workflow plan that describes a specific task performed by an Agent
terms.scopeNote: A workflow step usually involves some input information, material or energy needed to complete the step, and some output information, material or energy produced by that step.

terms.label: Subprocess
terms.definition: A process that is included within another Process.

terms.label: Task
terms.definition: An atomic unit of a task in a workflow procedure where one or more distinct, clearly defined actions are performed and may be characterized by a starting and ending time
terms.source: This Document, Usage notes adopted from https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_4299e344_a321_4ef2_a744_bacfcce80afc and https://www.irit.fr/recherches/MELODI/ontologies/BBO#Task
terms.scopeNote: The concept of task is developed in strict connection with the concept of workflow: a task is always part of a workflow and a workflow always possess some tasks. This makes the relation between task and workflow an holistic relation, with task as role and workflow as whole.

terms.label: The Handle system
terms.definition: The Handle System provides a general-purpose global name service enabling secure name resolution over the Internet, designed to enable a broad set of communities to use the technology to identify digital content independent of location. The DOI system utilises the Handle System as one component in building an added value application, for the persistent, semantically interoperable, identification of intellectual property entities. Notation: Handle

terms.label: Tool
terms.definition: Physical or digital resource that helps an agent perform an action
terms.source: Metadata4Ing: An ontology for describing the generation of research data within a scientific activity.

terms.label: Transaction
terms.definition: A cooperative interaction between two agents, involving the exchange or transfer of exchangeable products, services, rights, or funds or the processing of some request by one entity on behalf of the other
terms.source: Adopted from ISO/IEC TR 15067-3-8:2020 and ISO 6707-2:2017(en), 3.2.53

terms.label: Transaction Identifier
terms.definition: A global or local identifiers for a specific transaction

terms.label: Trigger
terms.definition: A specific event in a planned process that initializes a new workflow branch
terms.scopeNote: Newly created workflows initiated by a formalized trigger are referred to as branches.

terms.label: Uniform Resource Identifier
terms.definition: A Uniform Resource Identifier (URI) is a compact sequence of characters that identifies an abstract or physical resource. Notation: URI

terms.label: Universal Resource Name
terms.definition: A URI that identifies a resource by name in a particular namespace. URNs provide globally-unique names for resources as opposed to providing information about their location (URL). Notation: URN

terms.label: Universally Unique Identifier (Version 4)
terms.definition: Most commonly used universal identifier for machine-readable resources Notations: UUID, GUID

terms.label: Validation
terms.definition: A planned process with objective to check that the accuracy or the quality of a claim or prediction satisfies some criteria and which is assessed by comparing with independent results

terms.label: Value
terms.definition: An articulation that is by social convention understood to be potentially assignable to a variable
terms.source: Physicalistic Interpretation of Modelling and Simulation - Interoperability Infrastructure

terms.label: Voucher specimen
terms.definition: A specimen that physically and permanently documents data in  published literature by verifying the identity of the organism(s) used in the  study and by doing so ensures that a study which otherwise could not be  repeated can be accurately reviewed or reassessed.
terms.source: Master Glossary for DOI Museum Property Directives
terms.scopeNote: Rock and  mineral specimens may serve as vouchers to document the geology of an area.

terms.label: Workflow
terms.definition: A recorded sequence of connected steps, which may be automated, specifying a reliably repeatable sequence of operations to be undertaken during the lifecycle of data
terms.scopeNote: A workflow is a type of prov:Activity that has at least two procedures as proper parts. A workflow may be seen as an abstract model of real work.

terms.label: Workflow Action
terms.definition: An Event with at least one participatory Agent that executes a Task that typically defined in a Plan as part of a Workflow

terms.label: Workflow Branch
terms.definition: A new instance of a workflow that splits from an existing workflow triggered by a planned activity such as acquiring a new collection object from an existing one (subsampling). The new workflow runs in parallel and is optionally reconnected for mobilization purposes.

terms.label: Workflow Event
terms.definition: Something that happens during a process as part of a workflow and commonly affects the flow of the process.
terms.scopeNote: Here event is generalized to cover many things in a process, including the start or end of an Activity or a change in state of a specimen

terms.label: Workflow Management System
terms.definition: A system that defines, creates and manages the execution of workflows through the use of software, running on one or more workflow engines, which is able to interpret the process definition, interact with workflow participants and, where required, invoke the use of IT tools and applications.
terms.source: Workflow Management Coalition Specification Document Number WFMC-TC-1011.

terms.label: Workflow Phase
terms.definition: A distinguished part of a workflow comprised of a grouping of processes based on conceptual, thematic, functional and temporal criteria
terms.source: This Document with contributions from ISO 24635-1:2025 and ISO/TS 16710-1:2024
terms.scopeNote: Phases must be defined explicitly and unambiguously with minimal semantic overlap between phases belonging to the same workflow

terms.label: Workflow Tool
terms.definition: Device, system or software used by an Agent to perform specific workflow tasks

sources.title: Allotrope Foundation Ontology
sources.description: The Allotrope Foundation Ontology contains all triples of Allotrope Foundation Merged Without QUDT Ontology Suite (REC/2025/06) together with triples inferred with HermiT.

sources.title: ArCo Ontology - Architecture of Knowledge
sources.description: The ArCo module is the root of the network ArCo - Architecture of Knowledge. It imports all the other modules and models top-level distinctions from the cultural heritage domain.

sources.title: Art Glossary: Definitions of Common Art Terms and Techniques
sources.description: A glossary hosted and curated by the Museum of Modern Art, specifically in the modern arts

sources.title: Basic Formal Ontology
sources.description: The Basic Formal Ontology (BFO) is a small, upper level ontology that is designed for use in supporting information retrieval, analysis and integration in scientific and other domains.

sources.title: BPMN Based Ontology
sources.description: BBO is a business process ontology. The core element of BBO is a formalization of a BPMN 2.0 fragment (namely Chapter 10 of BPMN 2.0 specification). BPMN 2.0 is state-of-the-art meta-model of business processes.

sources.title: CHAracterisation MEthodology Ontology (CHAMEO)
sources.description: A semantic framework designed to harmonize materials characterisation methodologies. CHAMEO provides a standardized terminology and structure to model common aspects across various characterisation techniques, facilitating interoperability and knowledge sharing in materials science.

sources.title: CIDOC Conceptual Reference Model
sources.description: The CIDOC Conceptual Reference Model (“CIDOC CRM”) is a formal ontology intended to facilitate the integration, mediation and interchange of heterogeneous cultural heritage information and similar information from other domain.

sources.title: Contributor Role Ontology
sources.description: A classification of the diverse roles performed in the work leading to a published research output in the sciences. Its purpose to provide transparency in contributions to scholarly published work, to enable improved systems of attribution, credit, and accountability.

sources.title: Core Ontology for Biology and Biomedicine
sources.description: COB brings together key terms from a wide range of OBO projects to improve interoperability.

sources.title: Croissant Format Specification
sources.description: The Croissant metadata format simplifies how data is used by ML models. It provides a vocabulary for dataset attributes, streamlining how data is loaded across ML frameworks such as PyTorch, TensorFlow or JAX. In doing so, Croissant enables the interchange of datasets between ML frameworks and beyond, tackling a variety of discoverability, portability, reproducibility, and responsible AI (RAI) challenges.

sources.title: Darwin Core
sources.description: Darwin Core is a standard maintained by the Darwin Core Maintenance Group. It includes a glossary of terms (in other contexts these might be called properties, elements, fields, columns, attributes, or concepts) intended to facilitate the sharing of information about biological diversity by providing identifiers, labels, and definitions.

sources.title: Data Catalog Vocabulary (Version 3)
sources.description: DCAT is an RDF vocabulary designed to facilitate interoperability between data catalogs published on the Web. This document defines the schema and provides examples for its use.

sources.title: DataCite Metadata Schema
sources.description: DataCite Metadata Working Group. (2024). DataCite Metadata Schema Documentation for the Publication and Citation of Research Data and Other Research Outputs. Version 4.6. DataCite e.V. [https://doi.org/10.14454/mzv1-5b55](https://doi.org/10.14454/mzv1-5b55)

sources.title: DOLCE+DnS Ultralite ontology
sources.description: A lightweight, easy-to-apply foundational ontology for modeling either physical or social contexts.

sources.title: EDAM - Ontology of bioscientific data analysis and data management
sources.description: EDAM is a comprehensive ontology of well-established, familiar concepts that are prevalent within scientific data analysis and data management (both within and beyond life sciences and [imaging](https://github.com/edamontology/edam-bioimaging)). EDAM includes topics, operations, types of data and data identifiers, and data formats. EDAM provides a set of concepts with preferred terms and synonyms, related terms, definitions, and other information - organised into a simple and intuitive hierarchy for convenient use

sources.title: Elementary Multiperspective Material Ontology
sources.description: The Elementary Multiperspective Material Ontology (EMMO) is the result of a multidisciplinary effort within the EMMC, aimed at the development of a standard representational ontology framework based on current materials modelling and characterization knowledge. Instead of starting from general upper level concepts, as done by other ontologies, the EMMO development started from the very bottom level, using the actual picture of the physical world coming from applied sciences, and in particular from physics and material sciences.

sources.title: Experimental Factor Ontology
sources.description: The Experimental Factor Ontology (EFO) provides a systematic description of many experimental variables available in EBI databases, and for projects such as the GWAS Catalog. It combines parts of several biological ontologies, such as UBERON anatomy, ChEBI chemical compounds, and Cell Ontology.

sources.title: FRBR-aligned Bibliographic Ontology (FaBiO)
sources.description: FaBiO, the FRBR-aligned Bibliographic Ontology, is an ontology for recording and publishing on the Semantic Web descriptions of entities that are published or potentially publishable, and that contain or are referred to by bibliographic references, or entities used to define such bibliographic references.

sources.title: GConsent is a consent ontology based on the GDPR
sources.description: GConsent is an OWL2 ontology for representing consent for GDPR compliance. The ontology is based on an analysis of modelling metadata requirements related to the consent lifecycle for GDPR compliance. It allows modelling and representation of information related to compliance in an extensible and comprehensive manner.

sources.title: Gender, Sex, and Sexual Orientation (GSSO) ontology
sources.description: The Gender, Sex, and Sexual Orientation (GSSO) ontology has terms for annotating interdisciplinary information concerning gender, sex, and sexual orientation for primary usage in the biomedical and adjacent sciences.

sources.title: GeoCore Ontology
sources.description: GeoCore Ontology is a core ontology for general use in Geology. It contains a limited set of concepts that are shared among various subdomains of Geology. Having a common core set of concepts is key in order to integrate and develop knowledge bases in the domain.

sources.title: Information Artifact Ontology
sources.description: An ontology of information entities.

sources.title: International Council on Archives Records in Contexts Ontology (ICA RiC-O) version 1.1
sources.description: RiC-O (Records in Contexts-Ontology) is an OWL ontology for describing archival record resources. As the third part of Records in Contexts standard, it is a formal representation of Records in Contexts Conceptual Model (RiC-CM). This version, which is v1.1, is the latest official release. It is compliant with RiC-CM v1.0.

sources.title: International Virtual Observatory Alliance (IOVA) Provenance Data Model Version 1.0
sources.description: Describes how provenance information can be modeled, stored and exchanged within the astronomical community in a standardized way.

sources.title: ISO 12651-2:2014(en) Electronic document management - Vocabulary Part 2: Workflow management
sources.description: ISO 12651-2:2014 defines terms and concepts relevant to electronic document workflow management.

sources.title: ISO 16439:2014 Information and documentation - Methods and procedures for assessing the impact of libraries
sources.description: ISO 16439:2014 defines terms for impact assessment of libraries and specifies methods for such assessment: for the purpose of strategic planning and internal quality management of libraries; to facilitate comparison of library impact over time and between libraries of similar type and mission; to promote the libraries' role and value for learning and research, education and culture, social and economic life; to support political decisions on levels of service and strategic goals for libraries.

sources.title: ISO 17369:2013(en) Statistical data and metadata exchange (SDMX)
sources.description: ISO 17369:2013 provides an integrated approach to facilitating Statistical Data and Metadata Exchange (SDMX), enabling interoperable implementations within and between systems concerned with the exchange, reporting and dissemination of statistical data and related metadata.

sources.title: ISO 18461:2016 International museum statistics
sources.description: ISO 18461:2016 specifies rules for the museum community on the collection and reporting of statistics. It provides definitions and counting procedures for all types of resources and services that museums offer to their users.

sources.title: ISO 18530:2021 Health informatics - Automatic identification and data capture marking and labelling - Subject of care and individual provider identification
sources.description: This document outlines the standards needed to identify and label the Subject of Care (SoC) and the Individual Provider on objects such as identification (wrist) bands, identification tags or other objects, to enable automatic data capture using data carriers in the care delivery process.

sources.title: ISO 19101-1:2014(en) Geographic information - Reference model - Part 1: Fundamentals
sources.description: ISO 19101-1:2014 defines the reference model for standardization in the field of geographic information. This reference model describes the notion of interoperability and sets forth the fundamentals by which this standardization takes place.

sources.title: ISO 19104:2016(en) Geographic information - Terminology
sources.description: ISO 19104:2016 specifies requirements for the collection, management and publication of terminology in the field of geographic information.

sources.title: ISO 19126:2021(en) Geographic information - Feature concept dictionaries and registers
sources.description: ISO 19126 specifies a schema for feature concept dictionaries to be established and managed as registers. It does not specify schemas for feature catalogues or for the management of feature catalogues as registers. However, as feature catalogues are often derived from feature concept dictionaries, this document does specify a schema for a hierarchical register of feature concept dictionaries and feature catalogues.

sources.title: ISO 21246:2019 Information and documentation - Key indicators for museums
sources.description: ISO 21246 specifies a set of key indicators for assessing the quality of museums: — for the purpose of strategic planning and internal management of museums; — for reporting to stakeholders such as funding institutions, policy makers, or the public; — to promote the museums' role and value for learning and research, education and culture, social and economic life; — for comparing results over time and between museums.

sources.title: ISO 21506:2024  Project, programme and portfolio management - Vocabulary
sources.description: ISO 21506:2024 defines terms used in the field of project, programme and portfolio management.

sources.title: ISO 22932-2:2020(en) Mining - Vocabulary - Part 2: Geology
sources.description: ISO 22932-2:2020 specifies the geologic terms commonly used in mining. Only those terms that have a specific meaning in this field are included.

sources.title: ISO 24480:2024(en) Biotechnology - Validation of database used for nucleotide sequence evaluation
sources.description: ISO 24480:2024 describes a practical procedure for nucleotide sequence database evaluation and validation.

sources.title: ISO 24635-1:2025(en) Language resource management - Corpus annotation project management
sources.description: ISO 24635-1:2025 establishes a core model of project management for corpus annotation, to specify the work packages of project teams, required processes and deliverables.

sources.title: ISO 2789:2013(en) Information and documentation - International library statistics
sources.description: This International Standard provides guidance to the library and information services community on the collection and reporting of statistics.

sources.title: ISO 5127:2017(en) Information and documentation - Foundation and vocabulary
sources.description: ISO 5127:2017 provides a concept system and general vocabulary for the field of documentation within the whole information field.

sources.title: ISO 6707-2:2017(en) Buildings and civil engineering works - Vocabulary - Part 2: Contract and communication terms
sources.description: ISO 6707-2:2017 defines terms applicable to contracts and communication in relation to buildings and civil engineering works.

sources.title: ISO 9241-125:2017(en) Ergonomics of human-system interaction - Part 125: Guidance on visual presentation of information
sources.description: ISO 9241-125:2017 provides guidance for the visual presentation of information controlled by software, irrespective of the device. It includes specific properties such as the syntactic or semantic aspects of information, e.g. coding techniques, and gives provisions for the organization of information taking account of human perception and memory capabilities.

sources.title: ISO/IEC 23000-15:2016  Information technology - Multimedia application format (MPEG-A)Part 15: Multimedia preservation application format
sources.description: ISO/IEC 23000-15:2016 specifies the standard representation of the multimedia description information (MPDI) generated and used by an organization in the process of preserving a multimedia asset for the purpose of facilitating the exchange of multimedia content between archives or other stakeholders (e.g. publishers, broadcasters, service providers and the like), as well as subsequent preservation and use.

sources.title: ISO/IEC 5207:2024(en) Information technology - Data usage - Terminology and use cases
sources.description: This document sets out terminology and use cases for data use, sharing and exchange. This document provides use cases detailing various types of data usage from both historical and hypothetical perspectives.

sources.title: ISO/IEC TR 15067-3-8:2020(en) Information technology - Home Electronic System (HES) application model - Part 3-8: GridWise transactive energy framework
sources.description: ISO/IEC TR 15067-3-8:2020(E), which is a Technical Report, provides a conceptual framework for developing architectures and designing solutions related to transactive energy (TE).

sources.title: ISO/IEC/IEEE 24748-7000:2022 Systems and software engineering - Life cycle management
sources.description: The standard establishes a set of processes by which engineers and technologists can include consideration of ethical values throughout the stages of concept exploration and development, which encompass system initiation, analysis, and design.

sources.title: ISO/TR 14872:2019(en) Health informatics - Identification of medicinal products
sources.description: The purpose of this document is to describe the core principles and proposed service delivery model for supporting implementation and ongoing maintenance of IDMP terminologies.

sources.title: ISO/TS 16710-1:2024(en) Ergonomics methods - Part 1: Feedback method
sources.description: This document describes the “Feedback Method”, a method designed specifically to collect the contribution of machinery end-users by reconstructing and understanding how work is actually performed (i.e. the real work). This method can help to improve technical standards, as well as the design, manufacturing, and use of machinery.

sources.title: Lightweight Information Describing Objects
sources.description: LIDO is an XML schema intended for delivering metadata, for use in a variety of online services, from an organization’s collections database to portals of aggregated resources, as well as exposing, sharing and connecting data on the web.

sources.title: Master Glossary for DOI Museum Property Directives
sources.description: The official compilation of all the definitions cited in the DOI Museum Property Directives (Directives) and related guidance documents. This Glossary will be updated as new Directives are issued or updated by the Office of Acquisition and Property Management.

sources.title: Medical Subject Headings
sources.description: MeSH (Medical Subject Headings) is the National Library of Medicine's controlled vocabulary thesaurus. It consists of sets of terms naming descriptors in a hierarchical structure that permits searching at various levels of specificity. This thesaurus is used by NLM for indexing articles from biomedical journals, cataloguing of books, documents, etc.

sources.title: Metadata4Ing: An ontology for describing the generation of research data within a scientific activity.
sources.description: The ontology Metadata4Ing provides a framework for the semantic description of research data and of the whole data generation process, embracing the object of investigation, all sample and data manipulation methods and tools, the data files themselves, and the roles of persons and institutions. The structure and application of the ontology are based on the principles of modularity and inheritance.

sources.title: Modern Science Ontology
sources.description: Modern Science Ontology (ModSci) is an upper ontology for providing a taxonomy of research fields, or fields of science. It provides a hierarchical classification of various entities such as publications, events and scientists' research fields.

sources.title: NCI Thesaurus OBO Edition
sources.description: NCI Thesaurus (NCIt)is a reference terminology that includes broad coverage of the cancer domain, including cancer related diseases, findings and abnormalities. The NCIt OBO Edition aims to increase integration of the NCIt with OBO Library ontologies. NCIt OBO Edition releases should be considered experimental.

sources.title: Next generation Biobanking Ontology
sources.description: Next Generation Biobanking Ontology (NGBO) is an open application ontology representing contextual data about omics digital assets in biobank. The ontology focuses on capturing the information about three main activities: wet bench analysis used to generate omics data, bioinformatics analysis used to analyze and interpret data, and data management.

sources.title: Ontology for BIoBanking (OBIB)
sources.description: The Ontology for Biobanking (OBIB) is an ontology for the annotation and modeling of the activities, contents, and administration of a biobank. Biobanks are facilities that store specimens, such as bodily fluids and tissues, typically along with specimen annotation and clinical data. OBIB is based on a subset of the Ontology for Biomedical Investigation (OBI), has the Basic Formal Ontology (BFO) as its upper ontology, and is developed following OBO Foundry principles. The first version of OBIB resulted from the merging of two existing biobank-related ontologies, OMIABIS and biobank ontology.

sources.title: Ontology for Biomedical Investigations
sources.description: The Ontology for Biomedical Investigations (OBI) project is developing an integrated ontology for the description of life-science and clinical investigations.

sources.title: Ontology for Informatics Research Artifacts
sources.description: Informatics and computer science researchers usually contribute to scientific knowledge by delivering and tangible outputs, namely research artifacts. Typical examples of informatics research artifacts are software prototypes, datasets, ontologies, methodologies, frameworks. Computer science conferences such as ISWC, ESWC, and others have started to use resource tracks to allow for resource papers that describe these artifacts. The goal of the Ontology for Informatics Research Artifacts (IRAO) is to fill this gap.

sources.title: Ontology for Scientific Evidence and Provenance Information
sources.description: The SEPIO ontology is in its early stages of development, undergoing iterative refinement as new requirements emerge and alignment with existing standards is explored.

sources.title: Ontology of Precision Medicine and Investigation
sources.description: The Ontology of Precision Medicine and Investigation (OPMI) aims to ontologically represent and standardize various entities and relations associated with precision medicine and related investigations at different conditions.

sources.title: P-Plan Ontology
sources.description: The Ontology for Provenance and Plans (P-Plan) is an extension of the PROV-O ontology [[PROV-O](https://vocab.linkeddata.es/p-plan/index.html#PROV-O)] created to represent the plans that guided the execution of scientific processes. P-Plan describes how the plans are composed and their correspondence to provenance records that describe the execution itself.

sources.title: PATO - the Phenotype And Trait Ontology
sources.description: An ontology of phenotypic qualities (properties, attributes or characteristics).

sources.title: PAV - Provenance, Authoring and Versioning
sources.description: PAV is a lightweight ontology for tracking Provenance, Authoring and Versioning. PAV specializes the W3C provenance ontology PROV-O in order to describe authorship, curation and digital creation of online resources.

sources.title: Physicalistic Interpretation of Modelling and Simulation - Interoperability Infrastructure
sources.description: A mid-level ontology with a focus on documenting cognitive processes and epistemic metadata

sources.title: PROV-O: The PROV Ontology
sources.description: The PROV Ontology (PROV-O) provides a set of classes, properties, and restrictions that can be used to represent and interchange provenance information generated in different systems and under different contexts. It can also be specialized to create new classes and properties to model provenance information for different applications and domains.

sources.title: ProvONE: A PROV Extension Data Model for Scientific Workflow Provenance
sources.description: ProvONE, a standard for scientific workflow provenance representation, is defined as an extension of the W3C recommended standard PROV, aiming to capture the most relevant information concerning scientific workflow computational processes, and providing extension points to accommodate the specificities of particular scientific workflow systems.

sources.title: QUDT Quantity Kind Vocabulary Version 3.1.5
sources.description: Provides the set of all quantity kinds.

sources.title: Repository Asset Distribution (RADion)
sources.description: RADion, and the higher level vocabularies that build upon it, are intended as a model that facilitates federation and co-operation. It is not the primary intention that repository owners redesign or convert their current systems and data to conform to RADion, but rather that it acts as a common layer among repositories that want to exchange data.

sources.title: Schema.org
sources.description: Schema.org is a collaborative, community activity with a mission to create, maintain, and promote schemas for structured data on the Internet, on web pages, in email messages, and beyond.

sources.title: Semantic Sensor Network Ontology
sources.description: The Semantic Sensor Network (SSN) ontology is an ontology for describing sensors and their observations, the involved procedures, the studied features of interest, the samples used to do so, and the observed properties, as well as actuators.

sources.title: Semanticscience Integrated Ontology
sources.description: The semanticscience integrated ontology (SIO) provides a simple, integrated upper level ontology (types, relations) for consistent knowledge representation across physical, processual and informational entities. It provides vocabulary for the Bio2RDF (http://bio2rdf.org) and SADI (http://sadiframework.org) projects.

sources.title: terms4FAIRskills
sources.description: A terminology for the skills necessary to make data FAIR and to keep it FAIR.

sources.title: The Biological Collections Ontology
sources.description: The BCO supports the interoperability of biodiversity and biodiversity related data, including data on museum collections, environmental/metagenomic samples, and ecological surveys. A key aspect of the BCO is distinguishing among material samples (i.e. specimens), observing processes, and data about either of those entities.

sources.title: The Funding, Research Administration and Projects Ontology
sources.description: The Funding, Research Administration and Projects Ontology (FRAPO) is an ontology for describing the administrative information of research projects, e.g., grant applications, funding bodies, project partners, etc.

sources.title: The OPMW-PROV Ontology
sources.description: The Open Provenance Model for Workflows (OPMW) is an ontology for describing workflow traces and their templates based on the Open Provenance Model. It has been designed as a profile for OPM, extending and reusing OPM's core ontologies [OPMV (OPM-Vocabulary)](http://purl.org/net/opmv/ns) and [OPMO (OPM-Ontology)](http://openprovenance.org/model/opmo). Since 2013, a standard for provenance has been approved by the W3C. Therefore, OPMW has been updated to extend the standard ([PROV-O](http://www.w3.org/ns/prov-o)). It also extends the [P-plan ontology](http://purl.org/net/p-plan), designed to represent scientific processes.

sources.title: The Publishing Workflow Ontology (PWO)
sources.description: The Publishing Workflow Ontology (PWO) is a simple ontology for describing the steps in the workflow associated with the publication of a document or other publication entity.

sources.title: The WICUS Software Stack ontology
sources.description: The WICUS Software Stack ontology have been developed to describe the software elements of a computational resource. These descriptions can be used to describe both, the already deployed software components and the software requirements of a workflow. This ontology is part of the [WICUS Ontology network](http://purl.org/net/wicus).

sources.title: The Workflow Fragment Description Ontology
sources.description: The Workflow Fragment Description Ontology (wf-fd) is a simple ontology designed to link the common workflow fragments detected by applying graph mining techniques to a collection of workflows to the original workflow collection. That is, wf-fd links the common workflow fragments to the workflows where they appear.

sources.title: The Workflow Motif Ontology
sources.description: This document explains the ontology for the Workflow Motif catalogue described in [Workflow Catalogue]. The catalogue highlights the results obtained from a manual analysis performed over a set of real-world scientific workflows from Taverna [Taverna], Wings [Wings], Galaxy [Galaxy] and Vistrails [Vistrails]. Workflow Motifs outline the kinds of data-intensive activities that are observed in workflows (data-operation motifs) and the different manners in which activities are implemented within workflows (workflow-oriented motifs). These motifs are helpful to identify the functionality of the steps in a given workflow, to develop best practices for workflow design, and to develop approaches for automated generation of workflow abstractions

sources.title: USGS Thesaurus
sources.description: Topics and methods of scientific study carried out by USGS, with product types, scientific disciplines, geologic time, and types of institutional structure and activities. Broad and shallow, used to help people find scientific information.

sources.title: w3C Provenance Activity Type Codelist
sources.description: This value set includes W3C PROV Data Model Activity concepts, which are treated as codes in this value set. Some adaptations were made to make these concepts suitable values for the Provenance.activity element. Coded concepts are from PROV-DM and the display names are their counterparts in PROV-N (human readable notation syntax specification).
